guideTitle: 6 Best Ultrasonic Cleaners for Mouthguards in 2026
metaDescription: We compared six ultrasonic pods for mouthguards, night guards and retainers on frequency, UV lamps, noise, cycles and warranty to find an easy daily cleaner.
introParagraphs: A mouthguard or night guard is awkward to clean by hand, because the soft plastic holds odor in tiny grooves and a brush only reaches the surface. A small ultrasonic pod fills with water, shakes debris out of those grooves in a few minutes and is gentler on the plastic than scrubbing with paste. For anyone with tired hands, a one-button cycle is a real convenience.

We evaluated six 200 ml pods based on product specs and buyer feedback, comparing frequency, UV lamps, cycle options, noise level, tank material and warranty. The lineup runs from the 42 to 47 kHz auto-adjusting Zima to a 38 dB UV-C pod, and from a three-cycle touch-control unit to a certified IPX6 stainless steel model.
Use the picks below as a starting point, then work through the buying criteria and decision tables to match a pod to your appliance and your routine.

products.name: Beser 45kHz Ultrasonic Retainer Cleaner, IPX6
products.description:
The Beser is the most complete pod here on build and safety documentation. It uses 45 kHz dual-turbine ultrasonic technology with two transformers, a 200 ml 304 stainless steel inner tank and IPX6 waterproofing. The listing cites CE EMC, LVD, FCC SDoC, RoHS and UL62368 compliance, and it offers three one-touch modes that start with a 5 minute ultrasonic cycle.

The stainless tank is easy to wipe and does not stain the way some plastic chambers can, and the 39 dB noise level is quiet enough for a bedroom. The tradeoff is that the listing does not mention UV lamps, so it relies on cavitation alone. The dentist-recommended claim is marketing language that we did not weigh, and you should still follow your own dentist's guidance on appliance care.

Daily use is simple: fill to the line, drop in the appliance and press a mode. Compared with the 48 kHz Clelifove it runs a slightly lower frequency and has no UV, while against the under 38 dB UMPOPO it is a hair louder but better documented on certifications. It suits people who want a durable, no-fuss pod.
products.bestFor: Daily users who want a durable stainless pod with documented safety certifications.
pros: A 304 stainless steel tank wipes clean and holds up to daily wet use
IPX6 waterproofing adds protection against splashes during cleaning
Listed with CE, FCC, RoHS and UL62368 compliance for added assurance
At 39 dB it is quiet enough for a bedroom or a shared bathroom
cons: No UV lamps are listed, so cleaning relies on ultrasonic cavitation only
The 200 ml tank fits one appliance at a time, not a full set
Only three modes, so there is less choice than on the UV pods

products.name: Zima Dental Pod Ultrasonic Cleaner for Oral Appliances
products.description:
The Zima Dental Pod is built specifically for oral appliances: retainers, aligners, mouth guards, night guards, dentures and braces. Its frequency adjusts on its own between 42 and 47 kHz, and it offers a standard cycle for daily use plus a Max Clean cycle for heavier buildup after travel or a break in routine. The listing describes the design as non-abrasive and compact enough for a bathroom counter.

That focus means fewer extras. There are no UV lamps listed and only two cycles, so it is less feature-rich than the Cakiyn or Clelifove, and it does not give a tank volume in the listing. A 12-month warranty with a reply promised within one business day adds some reassurance, though the awards cited in the listing are marketing and we did not rely on them.

Ownership is a rinse-and-go routine that suits a bathroom counter. Compared with the Cakiyn at 42 to 48 kHz and three modes, the Zima has a narrower sweep and fewer options but a simpler decision. If you want UV or a longer warranty, the Clelifove at two years offers more.
products.bestFor: Guard, retainer and aligner wearers who want a simple, dental-focused routine.
pros: Frequency auto-adjusts from 42 to 47 kHz on its own during a cycle
Max Clean mode handles heavier buildup after travel or a missed day

A 12-month warranty comes with support replies within a business day
cons: No UV lamps are listed, so it relies on ultrasonic cleaning alone
Only two modes, standard and Max Clean, so there is little fine control
The 12-month warranty is shorter than the two years on the Clelifove

products.name: Cakiyn 42-48kHz Dynamic Ultrasonic Retainer Cleaner
products.description:
The Cakiyn sweeps through 42 to 48 kHz during a cycle, which the listing says spreads ultrasonic energy more evenly through the water. It adds four UV lights inside the lid and three one-touch modes: a 5 minute quick clean and a 10 minute deep clean, both with ultrasonic and UV, plus a 10 minute UV-only mode. A circular transparent window lets you watch the cavitation, and it includes precision tweezers and a microfiber cloth.

The frequency sweep is the main attraction, because a single fixed frequency can leave quieter spots in the tank. The tradeoff is the same 200 ml size as the others, so only one guard or retainer fits at a time, and the UV lights are an extra rather than a replacement for rinsing and brushing. The listing mentions 24-hour customer service but no specific warranty term.

Daily use is one press and walk away. It compares well with the 48 kHz Clelifove, which also has three modes and four UV lights but a fixed frequency, and it has more flexibility than the Zima at two modes. Choose it if you like to see the process through the window.
products.bestFor: Users who want a frequency sweep, UV lights and a viewing window in one pod.
pros: A 42 to 48 kHz sweep spreads ultrasonic energy across the 200 ml tank
Four UV lights and three modes give flexible daily and deep cycles

cons: No specific warranty term is listed, only 24-hour customer service

products.name: UMPOPO 48kHz Ultrasonic Retainer Cleaner with UV-C
products.description:
The UMPOPO is the quietest pod in this group, running under 38 dB on the listing's noise figure, and it combines 48 kHz ultrasonic cleaning with a UV-C lamp. Its longest program pairs 10 minutes of cleaning with 10 minutes of UV-C, and a pulse-flow mode alternates short bursts of cleaning with rest periods. The listing says it is portable enough to travel with.

The listing is inconsistent on mode count, mentioning both four and three modes, so we have not committed to a number. The tradeoff is clarity, because the pulse-flow wording is promotional and we did not weigh its claimed cleaning gains. Like the others, it holds a single appliance at a time, and UV-C is an add-on that does not remove the need to rinse.

It is quick to set up and easy to carry. Compared with the 39 dB Beser it is slightly quieter but lacks the stainless tank and IPX6 rating, and against the 48 kHz LOVELAB, which also uses UV-C, it offers a longer cycle. Choose it for a shared bedroom or travel use.
products.bestFor: Light sleepers and travelers who want a very quiet pod with UV-C.
pros: Under 38 dB makes it the quietest pod in this group on paper
48 kHz sits at the top of the range here, gentle on soft guard plastics
A UV-C lamp adds an odor-fighting step to the ultrasonic cycle
Portable size makes it simple to pack for travel or a hotel stay
cons: The listing is inconsistent about how many cleaning modes it offers
No stainless tank or waterproof rating is mentioned in the listing
UV-C does not replace rinsing the appliance after each cycle

products.name: Clelifove 48kHz Ultrasonic Retainer Cleaner with UV
products.description:
The Clelifove pairs 48 kHz ultrasonic cleaning with four UV lights under the lid and three one-button modes: a 5 minute quick clean, a 10 minute deep clean, and a 10 minute UV-only mode, all with automatic shut-off. It holds 200 ml, runs under 45 dB and includes precision tweezers and a microfiber cloth. The listing mentions a 2-year warranty and customer service.

The warranty is the standout, since it is the longest term in the group on the listings we reviewed. The listing says it works with just water, and better with a cleaning tablet, which is useful because plain water is the easiest routine. The tradeoff is that its 45 dB ceiling is louder than the UMPOPO under 38 dB and the Beser at 39 dB, and the pod is built for one item at a time.

Ownership is a one-button routine with a compact footprint for a bathroom or travel bag. Compared with the Cakiyn it offers a longer warranty but a fixed frequency instead of a sweep, and against the Zima at 12 months it offers twice the warranty term. It suits people who care most about long-term support.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want UV, simple modes and the longest warranty term in this group.
pros: A 2-year warranty is the longest coverage stated among these pods
48 kHz ultrasonic suits soft mouthguards and clear aligner trays
Four UV lights and three modes with automatic shut-off keep it simple
Tweezers and a microfiber cloth come in the box for daily use
cons: At under 45 dB it can run louder than the UMPOPO and the Beser do
A single 200 ml pod holds only one appliance at a time, not a set

products.name: LOVELAB 48kHz Ultrasonic Retainer Cleaner with UV-C
products.description:
The LOVELAB runs 48 kHz ultrasonic cleaning with UV-C modules in the lid and three timed cycles on a digital touch display, starting with a 3 minute quick rinse. The inner tank is food-grade SUS304 stainless steel with a 200 ml maximum. It is designed for retainers, aligners and similar oral appliances, and the listing includes clear safety notes.

Those safety notes are worth reading: do not submerge the unit, do not let water into the housing, and always add water before turning on the power. The tradeoff is that the listing does not give a noise figure or a warranty term, and its other cycle lengths are cut off in the listing, so we left them out rather than guess. Touch controls can also be less satisfying than a physical button if your fingertips are dry or numb.

Day to day it is straightforward and the stainless tank wipes clean easily. Compared with the UMPOPO, which also uses UV-C at 48 kHz, it offers a clearer three-cycle display and a stainless tank. Against the Beser at 45 kHz it lacks the IPX6 and certification detail, but it adds UV.
products.bestFor: People who like a digital display and a quick 3 minute rinse option.
pros: A 3 minute quick cycle suits a fast daily rinse of a night guard
The food-grade SUS304 stainless tank is easy to wipe and durable

buyingCriteria.explanation: Mouthguards, night guards and aligners are soft plastics, so a gentle frequency is preferable to the harsher 40 kHz range of workshop machines. Most dental pods run between 42 and 48 kHz. In this lineup the LOVELAB, UMPOPO and Clelifove run at 48 kHz, the Beser at 45 kHz, the Cakiyn sweeps 42 to 48 kHz and the Zima adjusts between 42 and 47 kHz. Any of these suits appliance plastics, so choose on other features.

buyingCriteria.criterion: UV lamps and what they do
buyingCriteria.explanation: Several pods add UV lamps to the lid, but they are an extra and not a replacement for rinsing and brushing. UV mainly helps with odor and surface freshness, and the lamps only reach surfaces they can see. The Cakiyn and Clelifove each list four UV lights, while the UMPOPO and LOVELAB list a UV-C lamp or modules. The Zima and Beser do not list UV, so choose them if you prefer ultrasonic only.

A 5 minute cycle is usually enough for a daily refresh, with a 10 minute cycle for heavier buildup. Short cycles also protect small units from overheating. The Clelifove and Cakiyn offer 5 minute, 10 minute and UV-only modes, the LOVELAB offers three timed cycles from 3 minutes, the Beser offers three modes, and the Zima offers standard and Max Clean. For daily use, more options matter less than a reliable one-press routine.

These pods sit on a bathroom counter or nightstand, so noise matters. A figure under about 40 dB is close to a quiet room, and 45 dB is audible but not intrusive. The UMPOPO lists under 38 dB, the Beser 39 dB and the Clelifove under 45 dB. The Zima and Cakiyn do not give a decibel figure in the listings we reviewed.

All of these pods use roughly a 200 ml chamber, which is enough for one mouthguard, retainer or aligner tray. Stainless steel resists staining and wipes clean more easily than plastic. The Beser lists a 304 stainless steel tank, the LOVELAB lists food-grade SUS304, and the Cakiyn, Clelifove and UMPOPO give a 200 ml capacity without naming the tank material. If you wear a thick sports guard, check that it fits flat in the chamber.

Small ultrasonic pods run for years only if the electronics hold up, so a clear warranty is a useful signal. The Clelifove lists 2 years and the Zima 12 months, while the Cakiyn lists only 24-hour customer service. The Beser cites CE EMC, LVD, FCC SDoC, RoHS and UL62368 compliance, which the others do not detail. Prefer a stated term over vague support promises.

howWeEvaluated.title: Frequency and cleaning approach
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated frequency and whether the pod sweeps or stays fixed. The LOVELAB, UMPOPO and Clelifove sit at 48 kHz, the Beser at 45 kHz, the Cakiyn sweeps 42 to 48 kHz and the Zima adjusts 42 to 47 kHz. All figures are manufacturer claims, so we treated them as relative.

howWeEvaluated.title: UV and cycle options
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which pods include UV and how their cycles are structured. The Cakiyn and Clelifove list four UV lights and three modes, the LOVELAB and UMPOPO use UV-C, and the Zima and Beser rely on ultrasonic alone. We weighed UV as a bonus, not a core cleaning feature.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and daily comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated noise levels because these pods live in bathrooms and bedrooms. The UMPOPO is under 38 dB, the Beser is 39 dB and the Clelifove is under 45 dB. Pods without a stated figure were scored cautiously.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and safety documentation
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at tank material, waterproofing and certifications. The Beser leads with a 304 stainless tank, IPX6 and several compliance marks, and the LOVELAB lists a food-grade SUS304 tank. Listings that rely on marketing claims such as awards or user counts were not weighted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warranty and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated warranty terms and support promises. The Clelifove leads at 2 years, the Zima lists 12 months with a reply within one business day, and the Cakiyn lists 24-hour customer service. We did not rank on price figures, only on what each model offers.

faq.q: Which ultrasonic cleaner is best for a night guard?
faq.a: For most people the Beser at 45 kHz with a 304 stainless tank and IPX6 rating is the safest all-round pick. If you want UV for odor, the Clelifove at 48 kHz with four UV lights and a 2-year warranty is a strong alternative. The 200 ml chamber means a very thick sports guard may need a fit check first.

faq.q: Can an ultrasonic cleaner replace brushing my mouthguard?
faq.a: It reduces the need for scrubbing, but it should not replace your dentist's or the maker's guidance. Cavitation lifts debris from grooves a brush misses, yet you should still rinse the guard before wearing it. UV lamps on the Cakiyn, Clelifove, UMPOPO and LOVELAB are an extra and not a substitute.

They are a nice-to-have for odor and surface freshness, not a core cleaning feature. UV only reaches surfaces it can see, so the ultrasonic cycle does the real debris removal. The Zima and Beser skip UV and still clean through cavitation, so choose based on whether odor is a concern for you.

faq.q: Is a higher frequency better for mouthguards?
faq.a: Higher frequencies are gentler, which suits soft plastics, but the difference between 45 and 48 kHz is small. The Beser at 45 kHz and the LOVELAB at 48 kHz are both within a comfortable range. Cycle length, fit and noise will affect your daily experience more than a few kilohertz.

faq.q: How long should I run a cycle?
faq.a: A 5 minute cycle is typically enough for a daily refresh, with a 10 minute cycle reserved for heavier buildup. The Clelifove and Cakiyn offer both, and the LOVELAB starts at 3 minutes. Long continuous runs can heat small units, so avoid stacking cycles back to back.

faq.q: How do I look after the pod itself?
faq.a: Always add water to the fill line before turning it on and never submerge the unit, as the LOVELAB safety notes advise. Empty and wipe the tank after use, especially a stainless one like the Beser's, and let it dry with the lid open. Avoid hot water, which can warp some guards.

faq.q: Can I use it for other items?
faq.a: Several listings mention toothbrush heads, jewelry and similar small items, and the 200 ml chamber suits small things. It is not a replacement for a larger jewelry or tool cleaner, and soft or porous stones should stay out of any ultrasonic unit. Use the dental pod mainly for appliances.
